title: Myles Garrett reportedly traded to LA Rams in blockbuster deal | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: Anytime you see the Olive Garden set on a weekday, you know what that means. Something has happened, at least beyond the confines of 7:00 to 9:00 a.m. Eastern when we are on PFT Live. And today, as we were waiting for the news that AJ Brown will be traded to the New England Patriots, that hasn't happened yet. Boom. Another post June 1 transaction hits the radar screen. Multiple reports indicate that the Browns will be trading 2025 defensive player of the year Miles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. Now, Browns GM Andrew Barry says nothing is final and the talks are ongoing. And here's the reality. It can't be final until 4:01 p.m. Eastern today. If it's finalized before that, the Browns end up taking the full dead money charge under Garrett's contract in the 2026 league year. After 4:00 Eastern, specifically as of 401, that's when the cap charge is divided, not equally, but it's divided with the bonus allocation that they're already going to carry this year for Garrett. And then everything else hits the cap next year. Now, the Browns had said they weren't going to trade Miles Garrett, but the most important development of the offseason as it relates to Garrett was the decision as part of a contract tweaking to delay a $29.2 million option bonus from being due in March until a week before the regular season. That extended dramatically the runway for trading Miles Garrett. and that put firmly on the table the possibility of trading him after June 1 or more specifically after 4:00 Eastern on June 1. So, it's out there. It's been leaked to everyone. It's reported everywhere. This is kind of what happened with Max Crosby. It gets out there and is it finalized? Will it be finalized? Will he pass the physical? That's all TBD. Won't that be something if the Browns issue a TUR statement on Twitter tomorrow night that the Rams have informed us they're backing out of the trade? But it just seems like for something like this, horses too far out of the barn to go back in, especially when you consider that the Browns are getting not just draft picks. This isn't just f them picks. They're getting defensive end Jared Verse, who was the 2024 defensive rookie of the year, the guy that presumably was going to be the the centerpiece of that defense moving forward. It makes me wonder why the Rams would be willing to give up Verse for Garrett. You could argue that Garrett's better. He's better than most defensive players in the league, but Verse is just getting started. And no team knows a guy better than the team that employs the guy. I just wonder what's gone on that we don't know about that has made the Rams willing to say and perhaps eager to say see you later to Jared Verse. Either way, that's part of what the Browns get. First round pick next year and some more on top of that for Garrett. Consider this as well because I remember when he made his big push to get out of Cleveland Super Bowl week 2025 when we were in New Orleans and he showed up and he did the media rounds and he was making his case very very calmly, very simply that it was time for him to move on to a team where he could contend. They threw money at him and that ended it. But the money they threw at him was 40 million per year in new money average. That was the the highest rate for anyone other than a quarterback at the time. Well, since then, the bar has gone all the way to 50 million per year thanks to the contract the Texans gave to defensive end Will Anderson Jr. who's only three years into the NFL. So, I suspect that Garrett, who has a no trade clause, part of waving it very well may be this is the deal that I want coming through the door if and when that deal is done. But this is huge for Garrett and the Rams, especially when we consider that the Rams used the 13th overall pick in the draft, the bonus pick that they acquired from the Falcons last year, not on somebody who would help them get better right now, but on somebody who will ideally not play at all in 2026 or perhaps 2027, maybe even 2028. Now, they get somebody who's going to come in and make a difference. But it's not just Garrett, it's Garrett minus Verse. Could you have imagined if they'd gotten Garrett and Verse? So look, Garrett gets a chance to compete at the highest possible level. A team that was not very far away from getting to the Super Bowl. And most people believe if the Rams had made it to the Super Bowl, they would have beaten the Patriots maybe as soundly as the Seahawks did. Seahawks Rams were the two best teams in the NFL last year. And you could argue that it all came down to one moment, that crazy ass two-point play from the Thursday night game in December, the Terry McCaulay hotline game, as has been reported by us and others. And there's been no effort by anyone to refute that. That's how that play turned. The whole season may have turned on that, not as it relates to Seahawks Patriots, but as it relates to Seahawks Rams. That's how close the Rams are. Garrett is going to put them closer. Garrett had 23 sacks last year. And Garrett has done his damage. Think of it this way. He's been getting these sacks when he rarely has an opportunity to pin the proverbial ears back with a 14-point lead in the second half where the other team is in pass first, pass second, pass all the time mode, and go chase the quarterback. He's more likely to get that when he's playing for the Rams. The Rams have the kind of offense and the overall team to be in the lead far more often than the Browns ever were. Yeah, this is what Garrett's been waiting for. First overall pick in 2017. Spent his whole career with the Browns. The Browns had said multiple times, it wasn't just this year, it was last year, it was before that. Andrew Barry constantly saying that he's going to play his whole career in Cleveland, then he's going to go down the road to Canton and be put into the Hall of Fame. Well, there's been a detour just like the detour the Rams once took. They used to be in Cleveland. Then they went to LA, then St. Louis, then LA again. Now Garrett's going to LA from Cleveland. Wouldn't it be something if the Browns finally figure it all out and it's Browns, Rams, and the Super Bowl? I know that's ridiculous, but what's not ridiculous is the Rams getting over the hump. the Rams doing what they need to do to become the team that five years after the most recent Super Bowl win at their home stadium plays in the next Super Bowl to be played at their home stadium and pulls off what would be the third NFL championship or at least Super Bowl championship in franchise history and the one that Garrett has been waiting for. really does kind of have those Reggie White vibes. text: The 49ers messed up. They just let the Rams trade for Miles Garrett. title: BIG UPDATE on Brandon Aiyuk trade: Post-June 1
text: June 2nd is on Tuesday. That's a significant day for trades in the NFL. Just so happens that Brandon Aiyuk has posted again on social media. Maybe a teaser with Commanders colors. I I've no idea what the hell's going on with Brandon Aiyuk, but you should have an idea of how the post-June 1st designation works because it colors business in this league and it would color potential business with Brandon Aiyuk if the 49ers were to trade him. The league's financial year officially turns after June 1st. Whenever you cut or trade a player, anything that happens after the June 1st date, the financial ramifications of it are pushed back to the next season's books. Anything that happens before that June 1st date, well, you're probably going to be shouldering the financial impact in the previous calendar year. Now, there is a thing called a post-June 1st designation, but that is applicable only to cuts, releases. That means that you can see the post-June 1st benefit of pushing dead money, staving it off like a stiff arm, into the future, into the next season. You can do that for releases, so there's no reason to wait until June 1st for a release. If the 49ers were to release Brandon Aiyuk, they they they could have already done that. But, trades trades, since there is no post-June 1st designation for a trade, those can start happening with the financial benefits beyond 2026. Those can start happening after June 1st. So, say that the 49ers and the Washington Commanders have had a behind-the-scenes agreement to trade Brandon Aiyuk for a late-round pick swap. Something that could have materialized, and this is all just in theory, but could have materialized because the Commanders didn't have much 2026 draft capital to trade, but they are willing to run a swap or something nominal in 2027. Would have made no sense for the 49ers to trade Brandon Aiyuk ahead of June 2nd, which is coming up on Tuesday. Because the 49ers owe Brandon Aiyuk money on the salary cap that has already been paid to him, right?
